base_rationale: CAM (hi-res Cambridge Add. 1570 f106r, ~80 MP IIIF master) is recommended. On completeness it is decisively superior: CAM has 0 illegible tokens vs GG's 16 (GG's col-3 water stain destroys the right edge of vv.21-28). On uncertainty CAM is also lower (16.3% = 66/404) than GG (21.9% = 97/442), and CAM's residual uncertainty is lexical/orthographic at diacritic-level legibility, not physical loss. This RESTORES the GAPS source-map (Cambridge = primary Samuel witness, GG = second): the prior low-res pilot inverted it to GG only because CAM was under-imaged at ~1.6 MP; with CAM re-imaged at ~80 MP that confound is gone and the source-map ordering holds on the evidence.

metrics.lacuna_counts_note: lacuna_counts.gg=16 is reconciled to the authoritative evidence: 1sa1_witnessGG.json contains exactly 16 ⟦illegible⟧ tokens (col-3 water stain, vv.21-28: v21=2, v22=2, v23=2, v24=4, v25=3, v26=1, v27=1, v28=1), and the hi-res alignment now carries exactly 16 lacuna-gg rows (one per GG ⟦illegible⟧ token; none unaligned or dropped). cam=0 and both=0 verified from 1sa1_witnessCAM_hires.json (0 ⟦illegible⟧ tokens). A prior defect classed 3 of these GG physical-loss rows (v24 align rows 6 & 19, v25 align row 7) as 'disagree'; they are GG water-stain loss, now correctly 'lacuna-gg' and EXCLUDED from the aligned denominator. Class tally after fix: agree=209, disagree=258, lacuna-gg=16 (was agree=209, disagree=261, lacuna-gg=13).

definitions.strict: exact literal token-string identity / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs
definitions.skeleton: diacritic/order-folded + near-homograph-folded token equality (class==agree) / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs, full aligned denominator
definitions.both_confident: skeleton-equal / aligned pairs where neither witness flagged that token uncertain or illegible (gap/insertion cells and lacuna rows also excluded from this denominator)

delta_vs_lowres.method: Like-for-like: BOTH the hi-res and the low-res baseline are recomputed under the single set of definitions in metrics.definitions. Hi-res is derived from this file's own corrected per-row alignment classes (post FIX-1). Low-res is derived from 1sa1_collation.json's own alignment[] (that file is left UNMODIFIED): strict = count of rows whose literal gg==cam (both cells non-empty) over its (agree+disagree) aligned denominator; skeleton = its rows with class=='agree' over the SAME full agree+disagree denominator (NOT the reduced 326 segmentation-trimmed denominator the low-res file originally used); both-confident = each low-res aligned pair joined back to 1sa1_witnessGG.json and 1sa1_witnessCAM.json (LOW-RES CAM) uncertain[] token_index flags, keeping only pairs where neither side flagged that token (and both cells present), then class=='agree' over those. Low-res aligned denominator = 480 (agree 119 + disagree 361; lacunae gg15/cam5/both1 excluded). In the low-res alignment every class=='agree' row also happens to be literally identical, so low-res strict and low-res skeleton are numerically equal (119/480) under these definitions; this is a property of that baseline's data, not an error.

as_originally_reported_lowres.note: computed under the low-res file's own different definitions (skeleton numerator class==agree but over a REDUCED denominator 326 that excluded segmentation-surplus tokens; both-confident over a different 107/172 basis); NOT comparable to the hi-res figures or to the like-for-like low-res figures above — retained for provenance only.

delta_vs_lowres.interpretation: Like-for-like (identical definitions for both resolutions): strict 24.79 -> 32.55 (+7.76 pts), skeleton 24.79 -> 44.75 (+19.96 pts), both-confident 49.42 -> 73.05 (+23.63 pts). DIRECTION CORRECTION: the earlier delta block claimed skeleton FELL -8.29 pts; that was an artifact of comparing the hi-res skeleton against the low-res file's reduced-denominator (326) skeleton. Under one consistent definition the like-for-like skeleton in fact ROSE +19.96 pts. So re-imaging CAM (uncertainty ~44%->~16%, its low-res illegibles resolved) DID lift agreement materially — the resolution confound was real and is now removed. But removing it did NOT collapse the disagreement: on text BOTH scribes read confidently the witnesses still agree only 73.05% (≈26.95% genuine divergence), and even the orthography-folded skeleton over the full aligned denominator is still only 44.75% (≈55% of aligned token slots differ at the word level). The honest thesis holds against the recomputed like-for-like numbers: GG (Gunda Gundē) and CAM (Cambridge) are materially distinct recensional/scribal text-forms of 1 Samuel 1 (word order, lexical choice, contraction, divergent name spelling, segmentation) — not one text imaged at two resolutions. Higher fidelity sharpened and explained the divergence; it did not erase it. semantic_pass remains 100% (28/28): every verse still tells the same Hannah-narrative episode — the divergence is textual-critical (recensional wording), not a difference in narrative content, and is not a catastrophe for the calibration.
delta_vs_lowres.asymmetry_note: Fidelity asymmetry has REVERSED relative to the low-res pilot: CAM is now the higher-resolution witness (~80 MP, 0 illegible, 16.3% uncertainty, diacritic-level legible) while GG is the lower-resolution side (~5 MP, 21.9% uncertainty). The residual asymmetry is now in GG's disfavor: GG's col-3 water stain yields exactly 16 illegible tokens across vv.21-28 (classed lacuna-gg and EXCLUDED from every agreement denominator); CAM has 0. The both-confident metric excludes every flagged/illegible/gap token on either side, so the headline skeleton and both-confident figures are not inflated or deflated by this one-sided damage; the ≈27% both-confident disagreement is genuine scribal/recensional variance, not GG damage.
